articleHeadline: Parasitic Brain Infection Recreated in Rats Mirrors Human
articleSummary: Extraparenchymal neurocysticercosis, a Taenia solium brain infection, is faithfully reproduced in a rat model using Taenia crassiceps cysticerci injected into the cisterna magna. Using a 0.25‑T scanner, 189 rats (63%) showed intracranial abnormalities, chiefly ventricular enlargement with cisternal dilation. The cisterna magna was affected in 85.2%, basal cisterns in 78.8%, with additional involvement of peritruncal cisterns and the spinal canal; subcutaneous cysts appeared in 39.2%. The frontal horn ratio averaged 0.62 ± 0.13 (range 0.28–0.92), roughly double the human hydrocephalus threshold of 0.3. The authors emphasize the model’s fidelity to human disease, including inflammatory dynamics that complicate therapy with corticosteroids and cysticidal drugs.

articleSummary: ALTNV, the Asian longhorned tick nairovirus, identified in China as a potential modifier of Dabie bandavirus–associated severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS). Screening 47,428 ticks from 15 Chinese provinces found ALTNV RNA in 1.29% of ticks, up to 1.75% in Haemaphysalis longicornis; the tick species can transmit the virus to mice, suggesting natural circulation via ticks. articleHeadline: Hepatitis A Immunity Stays High in Urban India While Hepatitis E Exposure
articleSummary: In urban Vellore, southern India, IgG serology for hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis E virus (HEV) was measured in two cross-sectional cohorts (2013: n=600; 2022: n=558), ages 1–40. HAV immunity remained highly endemic and uniform across years: seroprevalence >80% among 1–5-year-olds and 100% by age 16+, with no statistically significant year-to-year differences. HEV exposure stayed low in youth and increased gradually with age; among adults 26–40, seroprevalence rose from 18% (2013) to 24% (2022), a non-significant change. Cluster analyses showed HAV seroprevalence was uniformly high across neighborhoods, while HEV exposure was low and heterogeneous, indicating localized risk factors. The estimated effective reproduction number for HAV (Re) was below 1 in both surveys, implying no sustained secondary transmission. Findings reflect a stable HAV-endemic milieu amid urban development and a patchy, slowly accumulating HEV exposure, with surveillance implications.
